61654-blackie-a-lost-cat-her-many-advent.title: Her Many Adventures
61654-blackie-a-lost-cat-her-many-advent.creator: Richard Barnum
61654-blackie-a-lost-cat-her-many-advent.description: A book by Richard Barnum. Blackie did not have so much as a speck, or a single hair, of white in her glossy coat of fur, and on a dark night, if you were to look for Blackie I think you would not have found her. For she looked just like a bit of the dark itself.

arxiv-1609-09243.title: Reheating constraints on Kähler Moduli Inflation
arxiv-1609-09243.creator: R. Kabir, A. Mukherjee, D. Lohiya
arxiv-1609-09243.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by R. Kabir, A. Mukherjee, D. Lohiya. The end of inflation is connected to the standard cosmological scenario through reheating. During reheating, the inflaton oscillates around the minimum of the potential and thus decays into the daughter particles that populate the Universe at later times.

arxiv-2110-08774.title: Nonlinear Transform Induced Tensor Nuclear Norm for Tensor Completion
arxiv-2110-08774.creator: Ben-Zheng Li , Xi-Le Zhao, Teng-Yu Ji , Xiong-Jun Zhang , Ting-Zhu Huang
arxiv-2110-08774.description: Abstract The linear transform-based tensor nuclear norm (TNN) methods have recently obtained promising results for tensor completion. The main idea of this type of methods is exploiting the low-rank structure of frontal slices of the targeted tensor under the linear transform along the third mode. However, the low-rankness of frontal slices is not significant under linear transforms family.

arxiv-2112-10988.title: Mapping industrial poultry operations at scale with deep learning and aerial imagery
arxiv-2112-10988.creator: Caleb Robinson, Ben Chugg, Brandon Anderson, Juan M. Lavista Ferres, Daniel E. Ho
arxiv-2112-10988.description: Abstract Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) pose serious risks to air, water, and public health, but have proven to be challenging to regulate. The U.S. Government Accountability Office notes that a basic challenge is the lack of comprehensive location information on CAFOs.

arxiv-2204-12896.title: Reflection positivity and infrared bounds for quantum spin systems
arxiv-2204-12896.description: Abstract Zusammenfassung The method of reflection positivity and infrared bounds allows to prove the occurrence of phase transitions in systems with continuous symmetries. We review the method in the context of quantum spin systems. Dedicated to Elliott Lieb on the occasion of his 90th birthday. Kapitel 1 Reflection positivity and infrared bounds for quantum spin systems Jakob E.

arxiv-2206-09182.title: Coin-Flipping Neural Networks
arxiv-2206-09182.creator: Yuval Sieradzki, Nitzan Hodos, Gal Yehuda, Assaf Schuster
arxiv-2206-09182.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuval Sieradzki, Nitzan Hodos, Gal Yehuda, Assaf Schuster. We show that neural networks with access to randomness can outperform deterministic networks by using amplification. We call such networks Coin-Flipping Neural Networks, or CFNNs. We show that a CFNN can approximate the indicator of a d d -dimensional ball to arbitrary accuracy with only 2 layers and 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathcal{O}(1) neurons, where a 2-layer deterministic network was shown to require Ω ⁡ ( e d ) \Omega(e^{d}) neurons, an exponential improvement (

arxiv-2210-04452.title: Bounds for canonical Green’s functions at cusps
arxiv-2210-04452.creator: Priyanka Majumder, Anna-Maria von Pippich
arxiv-2210-04452.description: Abstract . Let Γ \Gamma be a cofinite Fuchsian subgroup. The canonical Green’s function associated with Γ \Gamma arises in Arakelov theory when establishing asymptotics for Arakelov invariants of the modular curve associated with some congruence subgroup of level N N with a positive integer N N .

arxiv-2212-05192.title: Walkability Optimization: Formulations, Algorithms, and a Case Study of Toronto
arxiv-2212-05192.creator: Weimin Huang, Elias B. Khalil
arxiv-2212-05192.description: Abstract The concept of walkable urban development has gained increased attention due to its public health, economic, and environmental sustainability benefits. Unfortunately, land zoning and historic under-investment have resulted in spatial inequality in walkability and social inequality among residents. We tackle the problem of Walkability Optimization through the lens of combinatorial optimization.

arxiv-2305-13868.title: Walsh Meets OAM in Holographic MIMO
arxiv-2305-13868.creator: Charles Vanwynsberghe, Jiguang He, Chongwen Huang, Merouane Debbah
arxiv-2305-13868.description: Abstract Holographic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is deemed as a promising technique beyond massive MIMO, unleashing near-field communications, localization, and sensing in the next-generation wireless networks. Semi-continuous surface with densely packed elements brings new opportunities for increased spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) and spectrum efficiency (SE) even in the line-of-sight (LoS) condition.

arxiv-2402-12948.title: GumbelSoft: Diversified Language Model Watermarking via the GumbelMax-trick
arxiv-2402-12948.creator: Jiayi Fu, Xuandong Zhao, Ruihan Yang, Yuansen Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Yanghua Xiao
arxiv-2402-12948.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) excellently generate human-like text, but also raise concerns about misuse in fake news and academic dishonesty. Decoding-based watermark, particularly the GumbelMax-trick-based watermark (GM watermark), is a standout solution for safeguarding machine-generated texts due to its notable detectability.

arxiv-2406-12812.title: A second order approach to the Kato square root problem on open sets Thanks: The first-named author was supported by the Alexander von Humboldt foundation by a Feodor Lynen grant. The third-named author gratefully acknowledges financial support by the grant no. 2022-03342 of the Swedish Research Cou
arxiv-2406-12812.creator: Sebastian Bechtel, Cody Hutcheson, Timotheus Schmatzler, Tolgahan Tasci, Mattes Wittig
arxiv-2406-12812.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Bechtel, Cody Hutcheson, Timotheus Schmatzler, Tolgahan Tasci, Mattes Wittig. We obtain the Kato square root property for coupled second-order elliptic systems in divergence form subject to mixed boundary conditions on an open and possibly unbounded set in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} under two simple geometric conditions: The Dirichlet boundary parts for the respective components are Ahlfors–David regular and a quantitative connectivity property in the spirit of locally uniform domains holds near the remaining Neumann boundary parts.

arxiv-2411-10335.title: Current Flow in Topological Insulator Josephson Junctions due to Imperfections
arxiv-2411-10335.creator: Kiryl Piasotski, Omri Lesser, Adrian Reich, Pavel Ostrovsky, Eytan Grosfeld, Yuriy Makhlin, Yuval Oreg, Alexander Shnirman
arxiv-2411-10335.description: Abstract Recent experiments on planar superconductor-topological insulator-superconductor (S-TI-S) junctions, e.g., in Corbino geometry, have reported low-temperature nonzero Josephson currents in states with integer fluxoid (flux) induced in the junction by a perpendicular magnetic field. This effect was discussed in connection with Majorana zero modes localized in Josephson vortices of such junctions.

arxiv-2505-10131.title: Floquet topological phases of higher winding numbers in extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model under quenched drive
arxiv-2505-10131.creator: Rittwik Chatterjee, Asim Kumar Ghosh
arxiv-2505-10131.description: Abstract In this study topological properties of static and dynamic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger models with staggered further neighbor hopping terms of different extents are investigated. Topological characterization of the static chiral models is established in terms of conventional winding number while Floquet topological character is studied by a pair of winding numbers.

arxiv-2507-08235.title: InsightBuild: LLM-Powered Causal Reasoning in Smart Building Systems
arxiv-2507-08235.creator: Pinaki Prasad Guha Neogi, Ahmad Mohammadshirazi, Rajiv Ramnath
arxiv-2507-08235.description: Abstract Smart buildings generate vast streams of sensor and control data, but facility managers often lack clear explanations for anomalous energy usage. We propose InsightBuild , a two-stage framework that integrates causality analysis with a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) to provide human-readable, causal explanations of energy consumption patterns.

arxiv-2604-14634.creator: Nahyun Lee, Guijin Son

plos-pone-0353113.creator: Duc Khanh Nguyen, Thanh Tuan Tran, Van Sy Hoang
plos-pone-0353113.description: Admission NT-proBNP provides stronger prognostic discrimination than the AHEAD score for 1-year mortality in hospitalized acute heart failure: A retrospective cohort study

pmc-10539380.title: Epigenetic profiles of elevated cell free circulating H3.1 nucleosomes as potential biomarkers for non-Hodgkin lymphoma
pmc-10539380.creator: Priscilla Van den Ackerveken, Alison Lobbens, Dorian Pamart, Aristotelis Kotronoulas, Guillaume Rommelaere, Mark Eccleston, Marielle Herzog
pmc-10539380.description: During cell death, nucleosomes, the basic structural unit of chromatin, are released into the blood stream and elevated levels have been found in the plasma of patients with solid cancers. In this study, we demonstrate an increase in cell free circulating H3.1-nucleosomes levels in plasma samples from patients with hematological malignancy, non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), relative to healthy donors.

pmc-11516391.title: Applying foresight methods at the national level in the field of substance use: Experience from the DRUG-PREP project
pmc-11516391.creator: S Cosgrove, B Hauspie
pmc-11516391.description: This presentation will focus on the experience from the DRUG-PREP project. While foresight has been used in other sectors, its implementation in the drugs field has previously remained relatively limited. The application of foresight to the drugs sphere is important in recognition of the fast-changing and intersectional nature of drugs and addiction.

pmc-11638233.title: Design and control of a low-cost non-backdrivable end-effector upper limb rehabilitation device
pmc-11638233.creator: Fulan Li, Yunfei Guo, Wenda Xu, Weide Zhang, Fangyun Zhao, Baiyu Wang, Huaguang Du, Chengkun Zhang
pmc-11638233.description: This paper presents GARD, an upper limb end-effector rehabilitation device developed for stroke patients. GARD offers assistance force along or towards a 2D trajectory during physical therapy sessions. GARD employs a non-backdrivable mechanism with novel motor velocity-control-based algorithms, which offers superior control precision and stability. To our knowledge, this innovative technical route has not been previously explored in rehabilitation robotics.

pmc-11771255.title: Genetic engineering drives the breakthrough of pig models in liver disease research
pmc-11771255.creator: Chenhao Xu, Xixi Fang, Xiao Xu, Xuyong Wei
pmc-11771255.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Compared with the widely used rodents, pigs are anatomically, physiologically, and genetically more similar to humans, making them high-quality models for the study of liver diseases. Here, we review the latest research progress on pigs as a model of human liver disease, including methods for establishing them and their advantages in studying cystic fibrosis liver disease, acute liver failure, liver regeneration, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, liver tumors, and xenotransplantation.

pmc-12594978.title: An automated decision support platform for rural environmental adaptive design based on VAE-ANAS integration
pmc-12594978.creator: Nana Tang, Furong Zhi, Jiehua Sun
pmc-12594978.description: Rural environmental adaptive design faces significant challenges due to complex environmental conditions, limited infrastructure, and the need for sustainable development solutions. This research proposes an innovative automated decision support platform that integrates Variational Autoencoders with Adversarial Neural Architecture Search (ANAS) to address these challenges.

pmc-12617242.title: Hypopharyngeal Lymphangioma Causing Persistent Dysphagia in an Adult: A Case Report
pmc-12617242.creator: Maryann Zhao, Nabil F Darwich, Erica R Thaler
pmc-12617242.description: Lymphangiomas are rare in adults but have the potential to impede patients' swallowing function and obstruct their airway. Hypopharyngeal lymphangiomas can be difficult to identify because they do not always display the expected imaging characteristics and can fluctuate in size. Treatment using a transoral endoscopic approach can dramatically improve symptoms.

pmc-12651349.title: Information-Theoretic Medical Image Encryption via LLE-Verified Chaotic Keystreams and DNA Diffusion
pmc-12651349.creator: Ibrahim Al-dayel, Muhammad Faisal Nadeem, Yasir Bashir, Ayesha Shabbir, Geert Verdoolaege
pmc-12651349.description: We propose an information-theoretic encryption scheme consisting of a four-dimensional chaotic map driver in combination with a prediction model using an LSTM neural net to generate a keystream, which was limited only after passing a test based on the largest Lyapunov exponent (LLE).

pmc-12737320.title: Copper-Based MOF-Derived Core–Shell Materials via N/P/S Ternary Doping for Peroxymonosulfate Activation: Efficient Degradation and Removal of Sulfamethazine
pmc-12737320.creator: Haiyang Zhou, Zhijing Zhang, Shan Zhang, Xiaofeng Wu, Haitao Li, Yong Qiu, Lichao Nengzi
pmc-12737320.description: Sulfamethazine (SMT) contamination in aquatic environments and its propensity to induce antibiotic resistance pose critical risks to ecosystems and public health, necessitating effective remediation strategies. Here, we develop a MOF-derived copper core–shell activator, Cu-MOFs400@PSN, by coating a calcined Cu-MOF derivative (Cu-MOFs400) with a nitrogen/phosphorus/sulfur-doped shell and systematically evaluate its peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation performance toward SMT degradation.

pmc-12977836.title: The carotenoids metabolism during tomato fruit ripening: insights into multi-level regulatory network
pmc-12977836.creator: Junwen Wang, Yue Wu, Jihua Yu
pmc-12977836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Carotenoids play an indispensable positive role in human nutrition and health. Understanding the biosynthesis and catabolism pathways of carotenoids in tomato fruits has practical value and fundamental importance. Carotenoid biosynthesis and catabolism are developmental program regulated at multiple levels. In recent years, numerous studies have explored the dynamic interactions between phytohormones, transcription factors, and epigenetic modifications to establish a regulatory network for carotenoid accumulation. However, understanding the regulation of the diversity and complexity of carotenoid accumulation remains incomplete.

pmc-12992910.title: Redefining water scarcity through the integrated water strategic resilience index amid climate and conflict pressures
pmc-12992910.creator: Filippo Verre, Krishna Kumar, Ronny Berndtsson, Hossein Hashemi
pmc-12992910.description: Water scarcity is a dynamic condition influenced by a variety of factors, including environmental variables but also political, economic, technological, and social variables. This research reflects the intersection of natural resources, governance, and human systems. Redefining water scarcity is a crucial factor for greater sustainable management in the face of increasing climate variability and geopolitical stress.

pmc-13346372.title: Stereotactic body radiotherapy and other locoregional therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma in patients with cirrhosis: real-world treatment allocation, BCLC-stratified outcomes, and prognostic determinants
pmc-13346372.creator: Cyriac Abby Philips, Tharun Tom Oommen, Jose Paul, Rajesh Sasidharan, Arif Hussain Theruvath, Aryalakshmi Sreemohan, Ambily Baby, Rinu Mary Saji, Akshay Venugopal, Ajit Tharakan, Philip Augustine
pmc-13346372.description: Background and aimsStereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a treatment option for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients ineligible for thermal ablation or surgery. However, real-world evidence on how physicians select between locoregional therapies, the stage-specific outcomes of these treatment decisions, and the prognostic determinants that transcend treatment modality remains limited.
